correctness.rationale: Positive boundary density turns four supported dual-curvature normals into exactly four axis-parallel sides. The exact normalized facet formula and strictly increasing horizontal mass function force horizontal reflection symmetry. Rational algebra gives λ=(3+κ)/(2(1+3κ)) with sharp open image (1/6,3/2), and dFκ/dt=−(3κ+1)(9κt²+u²)/(t²(3κt²+u)²)<0, proving unique positive inverse. Exact symbolic checks and 16 independent angular quadratures corroborate formulas without replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating current theorems require general-position normal arrays or odd cardinality and hence cannot cover the four-direction antipodal cross. Existing even-data inverse results apply only B=C, not the genuine non-even target B≠C. Competing scalar quartic dual-volume, subspace concentration, and smooth-density solution-count claims do not entail the sharp non-even inverse theorem. Search limitation and historical priority are recorded.

value.rationale: The exact inverse of a natural non-even discrete curvature measure solves a sharp existence, necessity, and global uniqueness problem on a genuinely three-parameter family. The strict endpoints are achieved only as geometric degenerations; the constructive reconstruction is stable as a unique positive root of a strictly decreasing scalar function. These features are not a numerical table or routine fixed-parameter substitution.
